title: Jim Cramer On Micron (MU) & Intel (INTC): Nothing Is Working Despite Good Businesses & Strong Quarters
detail:
Jim Cramer On Micron (MU) & Intel (INTC): Nothing Is Working Despite Good Businesses & Strong Quarters
Ramish Cheema

INTC
MU

Semiconductor giants Intel Corporation (NASDAQ:INTC) and Micron Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ:MU)'s shares have ended the week as part of yet another historic bloodbath for the semiconductor sector. Both have lost roughly 12% over the past five days amidst a painful rout for the semiconductor industry that saw the close 9.9% lower during the same day. Cramer, who has been one of Intel's strongest proponents, discussed Intel and Micron in his morning appearance on the 12th:

"When you look at that chart, are those great companies? Yes. Are those companies that are for sale? Every one of them was on sale everyday. And we should include by the way, cause I've been recommending Intel to the club, because Intel was great and then Intel has been terrible. And I think that it's important David to point out, that these were the market leaders. I mean Micron apparently upped its buyback, or said it was going to up its buyback. Nothing. Nothing is moving these stocks. And yet you can move, ServiceNow with a feather.

"Well look, there'll come a time when we'll see the actual earnings, and I think they're going to be very impressive. But right now, people are saying, look, this is overdone. And they've been saying that. I happen to think having spent a lot of time with Micron in Boise. That Micron's going to have a really good quarter. But sometimes between now and the quarter you have endless selling. Intel has just been, straight down, from 115. And yet I understand that business is quite good.

"But people care ServiceNow's business is quite good more than they care about Intel."

While Cramer discussed both, only one stock featured on our list of the 10 Most Promising Technology Stocks to Buy Right Now - a list that looks extensively at analyst ratings to determine which stocks are hot and which are not.

Jim Cramer Sees a Telling Change in Broadcom’s (AVGO) Stock

As the stock bloodbath continued, Cramer briefly discussed Micron in a tweet:

"Micron bucking the SK Hynix curse for the first time...."

With both firms being chip companies, their narrative is similar on a fundamental level but differs in the specifics. Starting from Intel, the debate is about whether the firm will be able to carve out a larger portion of the AI pie for itself, given that its strengths lie with CPUs as opposed to GPUs, which are powering the current AI wave. Additionally, it also depends on the firm's foundry business, which is aiming to compete with Taiwan's TSMC in the global contract chip manufacturing industry.On the AI front, Intel's second quarter came with good news as the firm's data center and AI business (DCAI) which captures the impact of CPU sales to data centers, saw revenue jump by 59% annually to touch $6.3 billion. Additionally, the foundry business's revenue jumped by 31% to $5.8 billion to indicate that the firm was firing well on both fronts.Yet, the chip business is quite capital intensive and Intel has to invest if it's to carve out a space for itself in the industry. The impact of focusing on the growth is clear as well, since first half capex sat at $6.1 billion while management outlined that full year capex would sit at $20 billion. Not to mention, foundry operating losses were $2 billion and the firm recorded a $11 billion GAAP net loss in the quarter primarily due to a $12.53 billion non-cash mark-to-market charge tied to escrowed shares under the U.S. CHIPS Act agreement.Looking at Micron, while for Intel the debate is about the role of CPUs in the agentic AI space, for Micron, it's about the sustainability of demand and the potential of high prices to remain as mega players SK hynix and Samsung bring additional capacity online and China's CXMT pushes to produce more memory chips. Cramer's tweet about Micron is unsurprising, as he had commented in August that US would "rue" the day it let it in the markets. For his complete remarks, check out Jim Cramer Says US Markets Will Regret Letting SK hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY) In.Starting from the bullish view, Micron's core data center revenue surged by 10 times to touch $18 billin in its fiscal Q4, gross margin touched 87% and management outlined that 75% of fiscal year 2027 were already committed. The third bit is particularly relevant, as it raises the chance of order shifts if Micron is unable to bring additional capacity online - a costly endeavor which could lead to tailwinds in case of a memory price downturn. FY26 capex sat at $27 billion while the shares are down by 27% since their June peak.As for the valuation, Intel's forward P/E of 63 over Micron's 7 means that the former is very richly valued. Cramer disagrees with the valuation as he has remarked that it should be higher. Read Micron (MU) Is A Stock Jim Cramer Thinks Could Go From ~$1,000 To ~$2,000 Per Share. While, as Cramer discusses in the piece, Micron's P/E suggests cyclicality, the ratio pencils in an earnings yield of 14%, which offers quite a hefty premium over risk-free assets. As for Intel, the picture is opposite as aggressive growth over little immediate earnings output is priced in. Looking at hedge funds, they're focused on the memory demand as opposed to CPU demand since 138 funds disclosed a stake in Intel in Q2 compared to 184 for Micron, according to Insider Monkey's data.READ NEXT: Jim Cramer Draws the Line on NVIDIA in China: Why National Security Comes First and Jim Cramer Defends His Dell Stance as Investors Complain About Missing Out.Disclosure: None.This article is originally published at Insider Monkey.

Key Stats for Intel Stock

Current Price: $89.85

Target Price (Mid): ~$390

Street Target: ~$118

Potential Total Return: ~336%

Annualized IRR: ~42% / year

What Happened?

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) CEO C.C. Wei signaled on October 15, 2026, that TSMC would support customers who cannot get enough capacity from the EMIB-T packaging of Intel Corporation (INTC). That puts a competitor directly in the path of the foundry business Intel expects to ramp first.

Intel closed at $89.85 on October 16, down 5.79%, in a broad chip selloff that took Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) down 5.95% and Arm Holdings (ARM) down 6.94%. Some outlets also tied Intel's drop to Wei's remarks. On October 14, an explosion at Intel's Kiryat Gat fab in Israel killed two workers, and as of October 16, Intel had not said whether output was affected. Intel reports Q3 results after the close on October 29, per its investor relations materials.

Intel Drawdowns (TIKR)
TSMC Offered Itself as the Backup to Intel's Packaging Push

EMIB-T is Intel's technology for linking AI chips and high-bandwidth memory inside one large package. Wei was answering Morgan Stanley's Charlie Chan, and he called TSMC's CoWoS packaging customers' first choice. TSMC's own lines are tight: in August, Taiwan's Economic Daily News reported some orders spilling from fully booked CoWoS capacity to Intel's Malaysia operations.

EVP and CFO David Zinsner said at an August 26 Deutsche Bank conference that packaging revenue should start ramping in the back half of 2027, ahead of high-volume 14A production in 2028. He expects it to run at around a 40% gross margin and 30% operating margin. Intel has not named a packaging customer, so that timeline rests on management commentary, not disclosed contracts. Intel Foundry lost $10.318 billion at the operating line in fiscal 2025, per TIKR.

Why Packaging Wins Could Delay a 50% Gross Margin

Zinsner still calls a gross margin starting with a 5 the goal, but said Intel is reticent to put a date on it because "some of our businesses actually don't get 50-plus percent gross margins, but they are really high-growth businesses." He put front-end foundry and advanced packaging at around 40% gross margin for now, and many custom ASIC products in the 40s as well.

Intel instead holds each unit to a "Rule of 45," where revenue growth plus operating margin should add up to 45, letting fast growers run thinner margins. Zinsner said not every unit will hit it next year.

Consensus already pencils in the level he won't date. Wall Street models gross margin rising from 36.7% in 2025 to around 54% in 2030, per TIKR, though only seven analysts publish 2030 revenue estimates. Each packaging win adds revenue near a 40% margin, and TSMC competing for the same customers could pressure that pricing. Intel's Q3 guidance midpoint of 42% is up from 39% guided for Q2.

Intel (NASDAQ: INTC) has been one of the market's big winners this year. The stock trades up about 170% year-to-date as of Oct. 14, 2026, compared to about 13% for the S&P 500. It could keep outperforming in 2027 for one reason: Intel's surging data center business.

Intel's data center and AI segment sells the server processors that power cloud computing and AI services. Its revenue grew 59% year over year to about $6.3 billion in the second quarter. That helped drive the company's strongest revenue growth in more than 15 years.

Demand for AI inference applications, including agents, could drive more demand for central processing units (CPUs), which is Intel's expertise. Inference workloads are boosting orders for server CPUs, and Intel expects industry-wide server processor unit shipments to grow by strong double digits through 2027, with momentum carrying into 2028.

Intel is also bringing better products to market. It launched its first server chip, Xeon 6+, built on its new 18A manufacturing process, and 18A production is running ahead of the company's internal targets.

The stock looks expensive, trading at about 47 times next year's earnings estimates. But Intel's earnings are recovering from depressed levels and are expected to grow at an annualized rate of 69% over the next several years. Relative to expected growth, the stock trades at a PEG ratio of 0.8, which looks attractive.

Investors will get an update when Intel reports third-quarter results on Oct. 29. If the data center business continues to grow at this pace, the stock could outperform in 2027.

title: Should You Buy Qualcomm Stock For Its Cash?
detail:
Should You Buy Qualcomm Stock For Its Cash?
Trefis Team

AVGO
NVDA
INTC
TXN

Image from Pixabay

Over the last twelve months, Qualcomm (QCOM) generated free cash flow equal to 5.5% of its market value. That outpaces the 4.4% yield for the median S&P 500 company. A yield above the median can mean a business that is either on sale or expected to shrink. Qualcomm's revenue fell in each of its last two quarters. So is that cash the sign of a business on sale, or of one that is shrinking?

What A Qualcomm Share Gives You

Free cash flow represents the money Qualcomm retains from operations after covering plants and equipment. Every share provides a claim on that cash. Just like a share of the profits, that claim holds up whether the company distributes the cash or holds it. Any cash Qualcomm keeps remains the property of its shareholders.

Share prices generally rise to reflect the cash investors can see. They climb even faster when that cash pool is growing. For Qualcomm, the trajectory of its cash matters just as much as the total amount.

When Qualcomm is a large share of what you own, your plan leans on one company's cash flow. See how to protect a concentrated position.

How Qualcomm Earns From Chips And What It Owes

Qualcomm licenses its patents and sells chips for phones, cars and other devices. In fiscal 2025, the chip business brought in $38.4 billion of the company's $44.3 billion in revenue.

The company spends little to maintain these operations. Capital spending consumed just 16% of its cash from operations over the last twelve months. The $10.4 billion left over equalled 23.6% of revenue. While Qualcomm has kept its free cash flow above zero in every twelve-month period since mid-2023, the total has shrunk for two consecutive years. It hit $12.6 billion in the twelve months to June 2024, fell to $11.6 billion a year later and dropped to $10.4 billion in the twelve months to June 2026.

At the end of June 2026, Qualcomm owed $15.3 billion against $8.3 billion in cash and short-term investments. That gap equals 3.7% of its market value. Over the last twelve months, operating profit was 14.9 times interest costs.

Why Investors Doubt Qualcomm's Phone Chip Business

Qualcomm's revenue has started to fall, which may help explain why its yield sits above the median.
After dropping 3.5% in fiscal Q2, revenue fell another 4.0% from a year earlier in fiscal Q3 2026. The operating margin also narrowed, slipping to 23.3% over the last twelve months from 28.2% a year earlier.

On the July 29, 2026 call, management said its phone chip sales reflected the effect of industry-wide memory prices on the smartphone market. Because of those prices and other input costs, chip gross margins will fall slightly below their usual range, management said. Qualcomm also said its share of the next iPhone launch would be materially lower than its earlier estimate of 20%. Moving forward, management forecast that revenue from Apple products would start stepping down faster in fiscal Q4 2026.

A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after investors weighed escalating borrowing costs and Federal Reserve remarks emphasizing price stability over rate cut signals.

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh stressed that maintaining price stability remains the central bank's primary mandate, while deliberately avoiding signals regarding the future trajectory of interest rates following an earlier rate hike. The prospect of persistent higher borrowing costs creates significant friction for high-growth sectors, particularly artificial intelligence and semiconductor firms that require substantial capital expenditure to finance advanced chip design, research, and fabrication infrastructure. Higher interest rates also reduce the present value of projected long-term cash flows, prompting investors to reassess rich valuations across technology equities.

Consequently, market participants adopted a cautious stance, triggering broad-based downward pressure and heightened volatility throughout the chipmaking ecosystem as financing conditions tighten.

title: Will Intel (INTC) Beat Estimates Again in Its Next Earnings Report?

Will Intel (INTC) Beat Estimates Again in Its Next Earnings Report?
Zacks Equity Research
Fri, October 16, 2026 at 8:10 AM MST 3 min read
INTC
Trade Intel on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Looking for a stock that has been consistently beating earnings estimates and might be well positioned to keep the streak alive in its next quarterly report? Intel (INTC), which belongs to the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry, could be a great candidate to consider.

When looking at the last two reports, this world's largest chipmaker has recorded a strong streak of surpassing earnings estimates. The company has topped estimates by 1,450.00%, on average, in the last two quarters.

For the most recent quarter, Intel was expected to post earnings of $0.21 per share, but it reported $0.42 per share instead, representing a surprise of 100.00%. For the previous quarter, the consensus estimate was $0.01 per share, while it actually produced $0.29 per share, a surprise of 2,800.00%.

Price and EPS Surprise

For Intel, estimates have been trending higher, thanks in part to this earnings surprise history. And when you look at the stock's positive Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction), it's a great indicator of a future earnings beat, especially when combined with its solid Zacks Rank.

Our research shows that stocks with the combination of a positive Earnings ESP and a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) or better produce a positive surprise nearly 70% of the time. In other words, if you have 10 stocks with this combination, the number of stocks that beat the consensus estimate could be as high as seven.

The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a version of the Zacks Consensus whose definition is related to change. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.

Intel currently has an Earnings ESP of +1.11%, which suggests that analysts have recently become bullish on the company's earnings prospects. This positive Earnings ESP when combined with the stock's Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) indicates that another beat is possibly around the corner. We expect the company's next earnings report to be released on October 29, 2026.

When the Earnings ESP comes up negative, investors should note that this will reduce the predictive power of the metric. But, a negative value is not indicative of a stock's earnings miss.

Many companies end up beating the consensus EPS estimate, though this is not the only reason why their shares gain. Additionally, some stocks may remain stable even if they end up missing the consensus estimate.

Cerebras CBRS shares have plunged 25.3% in the past month, underperforming the broader Zacks Business Services sector, which returned 0.3%.

The company's shares have also underperformed its competitors, which include NVIDIA NVDA, Advanced Micro Devices AMD, and Intel INTC in the AI space. Shares of NVIDIA and Advanced Micro Devices gained 1.6% and 9.7%, respectively, while Intel lost 5.6% over the past month.

The underperformance can be attributed to near-term margin pressure from higher costs associated with renting back systems to expand its cloud capacity. Data center availability constraints and deployment delays could limit revenue growth, while significant investments in manufacturing and infrastructure weigh on profitability. Heavy dependence on OpenAI poses customer concentration risks.

CBRS Stock Performance
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

However, Cerebras is benefiting from surging demand for high-speed AI inference, expanding cloud deployments and strategic partnerships with hyperscalers. Growing data center capacity, manufacturing expansion and a strong backlog are supporting its long-term growth prospects.

CBRS Benefits From Strong AI Demand and Backlog Growth

Cerebras is benefiting from robust demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, driven by the rapid adoption of high-speed inference across enterprises, hyperscalers and AI developers. The company's second-quarter 2026 core revenues surged 103% year over year to $209.9 million, reflecting strong demand for its AI computing solutions. Core cloud and other services revenues jumped 287% to $127.7 million, supported by expanding OpenAI deployments and increased cloud customer usage.

The company is aggressively expanding its data center footprint to capitalize on increasing AI infrastructure investments. The company secured more than 600 megawatts of data center capacity, either operational or under contract for delivery by the end of 2027. Its manufacturing expansion initiatives, supported by partnerships with Flex, Sanmina and TSMC, are expected to increase manufacturing capacity by more than tenfold in 2026. These investments position Cerebras to address growing customer demand and accelerate revenue growth.

Strategic collaborations with OpenAI, Amazon Web Services (AWS) and other hyperscalers further strengthen Cerebras' growth prospects. Its partnership with OpenAI is supporting strong demand for high-speed AI inference, while AWS integration through Amazon Bedrock, expected to become generally available in the first quarter of 2027, should expand enterprise adoption. Growing customer engagements across AI coding, agentic workflows and cybersecurity provide additional opportunities to diversify its revenue streams.

Cerebras' strong backlog also supports future upside. Remaining performance obligations stood at $25.4 billion as of June 30, 2026, supporting investments in infrastructure and manufacturing expansion. The company expects core revenues to more than triple in 2027, followed by significant growth in subsequent years. Expanding adoption across AI coding, agentic workflows and cybersecurity applications is expected to strengthen Cerebras' long-term growth trajectory.

Stocks closed lower on Wall Street as more drops for big tech companies weighed on the market.

The S&P 500 lost 1.1% Friday, and the Nasdaq composite sank 2.1%. Both posted their worst week since June. The Dow Jones Industrial Average didn't do as badly, and fell 0.3%.

Chip companies pulled back some more as worries deepened about how long the frenzy over the AI buildout will last. Micron Technology fell 5.6% and Intel lost 5.8%. European and Asian markets closed higher.

On Friday:

The S&P 500 fell 84.62 points, or 1.1%, to 7,659.44.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 175.28 points, or 0.3%, to 52,002.41.

The Nasdaq composite fell 572.99 points, or 2.1%, to 26,140.03.

The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies fell 45.90 points, or 1.7%, to 2,721.37.

For the week:

The S&P 500 is down 152.10 points, or 1.9%.

The Dow is up 347.46 points, or 0.7%.

The Nasdaq is down 1,226.14 points, or 4.5%.

The Russell 2000 is down 85.61 points, or 3%.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 813.94 points, or 11.9%.

The Dow is up 3,939.12 points, or 8.2%.

The Nasdaq is up 2,898.04 points, or 12.5%.

The Russell 2000 is up 239.46 points, or 9.6%.
